_comment: Real-world title pairs and how they must be judged.
This is the most valuable file in the repository. Every entry is a case
that a matcher can plausibly get wrong, and most were paid for by an
Adding a case is the easiest useful contribution you can make: append an
object with `a`, `b`, `verdict` and a short `why`. See CONTRIBUTING.md.
verdict is one of: same, different, uncertain
same       one file satisfies both entries
different  these are distinct recordings, or distinct songs
uncertain  a human or a catalogue lookup is needed; never guess

cases.b: Who Wants to Live Forever (Live in Budapest)
cases.why: a live recording is not the studio take
the word live is in the title itself, not a qualifier
two parts of a track are two recordings
the combined version is neither part
sharp s transliteration differs between catalogues
capitalisation only
both open with a number; a greedy track-number strip makes these BPM and Tage
a featured credit does not change the recording
a remix is a separate recording
different qualifiers on the same song
single and album cuts differ
a remaster is a distinct file even though it is the same performance
umlaut spelled out
short generic titles must not collapse together
generic titles still match themselves; artist scoping is the caller's job
a prefix is not a match
case only, and the bracket is not a recording qualifier
shares a word, different song
ampersand versus the German word
trailing dash qualifier, not a bracket
radio edits are shorter recordings
producer credit is not a qualifier
live venue qualifier
the album track covers both parts and satisfies neither entry alone
leetspeak stylisation; a matcher should not guess either way
off by one letter, plausibly a typo and plausibly two songs
